memory_update.text: DSGX should be carried forward as the highest-fit US-listed customs/regulatory-compliance software candidate for the tariff enforcement and traceability node.
ULS is a useful US-listed TIC reference anchor, but tariff-specific upside is an inference that needs evidence from certification demand, lab utilization, and supplier requalification commentary.

FCN and CBZ are underfollowed consulting-capacity hypotheses; both have explicit tariff/customs service offerings, but exposure may be too small relative to total revenue unless filings or transcripts show acceleration.
Many of the purest supply-chain traceability and trade-enforcement platforms appear private, including Altana; public-market mapping may require using broader software/data or advisory proxies.

Core falsification test: if tariff and trade-enforcement complexity rises but customs-filing volumes, denied-party screening, certification backlog, trade-advisory hiring, and compliance-practice utilization do not improve, the node should be downgraded.

node: Tariff, trade-enforcement, testing, inspection, certification, and traceability services
summary: Expanded the node around tariff and trade-enforcement compliance into a small US-listed universe focused on customs/regulatory software, TIC/product certification, and specialized advisory capacity. The strongest direct public-market fit found in this pass is Descartes Systems Group because customs/regulatory compliance and global trade intelligence are core product lines. UL Solutions is the cleanest US-listed TIC/product-certification reference name, but its direct tariff sensitivity is more indirect. FTI Consulting and CBIZ are underfollowed advisory-capacity candidates with explicit tariff/customs offerings, but exposure is likely small relative to total revenue and needs segment-level verification.
